title: Data and code for: Who's gonna feed the kids? Provisioning alternation in dunnock pairs and trios is largely explained by each parent's own visiting pattern
description:
Data, R code and Quarto manuscript source to reproduce every analysis, figure and number in Paschoaletto et al., Who's gonna feed the kids? Provisioning alternation in dunnock pairs and trios is largely explained by each parent's own visiting pattern.

The data are 4,376 provisioning visits in 297 nest watches at 163 nests of dunnocks (Prunella modularis) in socially monogamous pairs and socially polyandrous trios, filmed in the Dunedin Botanic Garden, New Zealand, over seven breeding seasons (2009/10–2015/16). The code computes provisioning alternation, five null models, same-day pseudo-pairs and a power simulation; analysis/run_all.R rebuilds all results and renders the manuscript.
